subject: science
passage: In a tropical cloud forest, the trees are wrapped in mist for much of the year. Mosses, ferns, and orchids grow thickly on the branches, and they do far more than ______ they comb tiny droplets out of the passing fog, and the water drips to the forest floor. In some cloud forests, this fog drip supplies a large share of the water that reaches the soil.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

explanation.why: "Mosses, ferns, and orchids grow thickly on the branches, and they do far more than decorate" is a complete sentence. "They comb tiny droplets out of the passing fog" is a second complete sentence that explains the first. Two closely related independent clauses can be joined with a semicolon.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Which" would attach the second clause to "decorate" as a description, but "which they comb tiny droplets out of the passing fog" has no place for "which" and makes no grammatical sense.
explanation.B: Correct. A semicolon correctly joins two closely related independent clauses.
explanation.C: Incorrect. With no punctuation, the two independent clauses run together (a run-on sentence).
explanation.D: Incorrect. A comma alone can't join two independent clauses; this creates a comma splice.
